james-bodnar.text: On July 22, 2025, Bodnar voted yes (4-0 roll call) to adopt the report for collecting FY 2025-26 capital charges on the property tax roll after no majority protest.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Water District Aug. 26, 2025 board packet (minutes of July 22, 2025 meeting)

james-bodnar.text: (2023) Bodnar was part of the unanimous vote for a "hybrid" pipeline-replacement funding plan: a $194-per-household annual charge on property tax bills plus about $24 million in bonds.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Board Votes on Hybrid Solution to CVWD Water Woes (June 2023)

james-bodnar.text: (2023) On choosing an auditor, Bodnar said the outspoken crowd "demanded choosing a company that charges 30% less"; the board selected SingerLewak.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Board Votes on Hybrid Solution to CVWD Water Woes (June 2023)

jeffery-w-johnson.text: On July 22, 2025, Johnson voted yes (4-0 roll call) to adopt the report for collecting FY 2025-26 capital charges on the property tax roll after no majority protest.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Water District Aug. 26, 2025 board packet (minutes of July 22, 2025 meeting)

jeffery-w-johnson.text: (2023) Johnson was part of the unanimous vote for a "hybrid" pipeline-replacement funding plan: a $194-per-household annual charge on property tax bills plus about $24 million in bonds.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Board Votes on Hybrid Solution to CVWD Water Woes (June 2023)

jeffery-w-johnson.text: (2023) Before the vote on the pipeline-funding charge, Johnson said, "We're all going to feel pain."

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Board Votes on Hybrid Solution to CVWD Water Woes (June 2023)

jeffery-w-johnson.text: As board president in 2025, Johnson said the board and staff "have held numerous workshops, surveys, interviews, open office hours and town halls" on operations and a possible rate increase.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: CVWD Public Meeting: Lots of Questions, Not Many Answers (June 2025)

alec-hyeler.text: (2024) Said his primary goal is "maintaining steady and affordable water rates" while ensuring water quality, and investing in long-term solutions "without burdening ratepayers, especially considering rising inflation."

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Water District Introduces Board Candidates (Oct. 2024)

alec-hyeler.text: (2024) Called climate change "undeniably one of the greatest threats to the future of our water district" and urged investment in conservation, recycled water and stormwater infiltration.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Water District Introduces Board Candidates (Oct. 2024)

alec-hyeler.text: (2024) Said CVWD "should avoid fearmongering and punitive measures, such as lowering rate tier thresholds" to educate the public about future shortages.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Water District Introduces Board Candidates (Oct. 2024)

alec-hyeler.text: (2024) Pledged "greater transparency to the decision-making process" and better ratepayer communication, including more board social media presence.

source.title: Crescenta Valley Weekly: Water District Introduces Board Candidates (Oct. 2024)

notes: Vote for 3. Incumbents Bodnar and Johnson: recorded votes found are unanimous (capital charges, 2023 pipeline funding plan); no 2026 campaign statements found. Alec Hyeler's only positions are from his 2024 CVWD run (CV Weekly questionnaire). No campaign statements found for Carla D. Dillon. CVWD's 2025 minutes list a Carla Dillon as the district's Director of Engineering and Operations, but there's no confirmation it's the same person, so nothing was attributed to her. Searches used: 4
